newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to impose tariffs on overseas rice.
newsitem.headline: Commission to impose tariffs on overseas rice.

text.p: The European Commisson will on Wednesday decide whether to impose safeguard tariffs on imports of processed rice from British, French and Dutch overseas territories, an EU diplomat said on Tuesday.
"The question is listed for Wednesday's meeting of the Commission and it is possible that they may decide on additional tariffs to protect European processors," the diplomat said.
The safeguard clause process was begun by the Commission in early December at the request of Italy, which expressed concern at rising levels of duty-free rice imports from overseas territories.
Duty free concessions were originally given to the territories to compensate for a reduced tariff quota awarded to ACP (African, Caribbean and Pacific countries belonging to the Lome Convention).
The ACP concession is limited to a 50 per cent tariff reduction up to an annual quota of 125,000 tonnes. But only 6,000 tonnes is expected to be imported within this quota in 1996/97.
Increasing amounts of rice from the ACP states of Guyana and Surinam were processed mainly in the Dutch Antilles before being exported to the EU, thereby benefiting from duty-free access.

According to the Italian complaint, rice imports from overseas territories between 1992 and 1995 passed the 58,000 tonnes anticipated in the market access agreement and has reached 192,000 tonnes annually.
